questions.q: What does the backward pass of training compute?
options: New training data
The gradient of the loss with respect to every weight
The final accuracy on the test set
The number of hidden layers to use
questions.explain: Backpropagation applies the chain rule from the loss backward to get the gradient for each weight.

questions.q: In gradient descent, how is each weight updated?
options: It is set to the gradient
It is increased by the gradient times the learning rate
It is decreased by the learning rate times the gradient
It is reset to a new random value
questions.explain: Weights step opposite the gradient (downhill on the loss), scaled by the learning rate.

questions.q: In the lesson, the analytic and numerical gradients agreed to about nine digits. What does this show?
options: The backpropagation code is correct
The model will not overfit
The learning rate is optimal
The dataset is noise-free
questions.explain: A gradient check compares the hand-written (analytic) gradient to a numerical estimate; agreement confirms the backward pass.

questions.q: With the same network, a learning rate of 0.5 gave a loss of nan after 300 epochs. Why?
options: The steps were too large, so the loss diverged
The learning rate was too small to make progress
The data had missing values
Tanh cannot be used with a large learning rate on any data
questions.explain: An overly large learning rate overshoots the minimum, and the loss and weights blow up.

options: One update of a single weight
One layer of the network
One full pass over the training data
The final loss value
questions.explain: An epoch is one complete pass through the training data (in full-batch training, one gradient update).
